title: Construction of the canonical formal push-pull comparison
statement: Let Y be a Noetherian scheme, J a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on Y, f:X\to Y a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], G a coherent J-adic formal system on Y and F a coherent module on X [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, pqf-def-coherent]. Fix an adjunction a:f^*\dashv f_* for tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and an isomorphism \beta:(f^*G_n)_n\simeq(F/(J\mathcal O_X)^{n+1}F)_n. Assume H=f_*F is coherent, and write \pi^J_n:H\to H/J^{n+1}H and \pi^I_n:F\to F/(J\mathcal O_X)^{n+1}F for the quotient projections. There exist a map of inverse systems \kappa:H^\wedge\to(f_*(F/(J\mathcal O_X)^{n+1}F))_n and a map \alpha:G\to H^\wedge of coherent formal modules such that for every n\ge0, \pi^J_n\kappa_n=f_*(\pi^I_n) and \alpha_n\kappa_n=\eta_{G_n}f_*(\beta_n), where \eta is the unit of a and juxtaposition denotes composition in diagrammatic order. No exceptional ideal or annihilation hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088B; first half of the proof: construction and uniqueness of alpha, parent proof steps 3--5

proof.text: Use coherence of H=f_*F on the Noetherian base to obtain quasi-coherence. The ideal-power pullback-image identity identifies the image of f*(J^(n+1)H -> H) with (J O_X)^(n+1)f*H. The latter inclusion followed by the adjunction counit f*H -> F and the quotient projection is zero by formalModuleQuotient_map_zero. Factoring through the image and the adjunction hom-set equivalence therefore shows J^(n+1)H -> H -> f_*(F/(J O_X)^(n+1)F) is zero. Define kappa_n by cokernel.desc. The cokernel factorization equation gives its required quotient identity, and cancellation of quotient projections proves naturality with respect to all transitions.

Define gamma_n as the adjunction unit at G_n followed by f_*(beta_n). Naturality of the unit and beta gives an inverse-system morphism gamma. Apply the compatible-map lifting lemma to the explicitly constructed kappa and gamma. Evaluating the equality alpha.hom >> kappa = gamma at op n gives precisely the second asserted equation; combine it with the cokernel equations for kappa.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull), first half of proof, construction of alpha from lim gamma; checked against https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088B

lean.statement:
theorem exists_formalSystemsPushPull_comparison {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (adj : Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f ⊣ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f)
    (G : CoherentFormalModule Y J) (F : CoherentModules X)
    (β : G.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f ≅
      formalCompletionSystem (J.comap f) F.obj)
    (h : RingedSpace.IsCoherent Y.toRingedSpace
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj)) :
    ∃ κ : formalCompletionSystem J ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj) ⟶
          formalCompletionSystem (J.comap f) F.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pushforward f,
        ∃ α : G ⟶ (completion Y J).obj
            ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj, h⟩,
          (∀ n : ℕ,
            formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F.obj) ≫
              κ.app (op n) =
            (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).map
              (formalModuleQuotientπ (J.comap f) (n + 1) F.obj)) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ, α.hom.app (op n) ≫ κ.app (op n) =
            adj.unit.app (G.obj.obj (op n)) ≫
              (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).map (β.hom.app (op n)))
